layers.note: The commonest shrub of lowland conifer forest, often a continuous layer under Douglas-fir and hemlock.

moisture.note: Dry to moist ground; thickest on well-drained slopes and absent from saturated soil.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 800 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Holds steep banks and road cuts.

shade_tolerance.note: Grows in shade or sun; densest under broken canopy.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS).
